summary: Both T81 repairs are confirmed. The cost property holds: the `!` gate move is behaviour-preserving (17 of 19 prior matrices byte-identical to five prior rounds), the load-bearing `]` fact was verified from the pattern rather than the prose (fuzz over 237186 generated keys, zero containing `]`), the disjointness consequence was independently re-derived and found correct with a tighter bound than the file states, and no shape I could construct grows faster than its size: 22 shapes x 4 sizes gave exponents 0.73-1.44 with `overOneSecond: []`, and six attacker-controlled dials swept at a constant 262144 bytes moved cost by a total spread of at most 36.1 ms. Duplicate handling is closed for all six T78 spellings plus eleven more, in both orders, at all four public boundaries, and the stronger form is the right call: the benign corpus is byte-identical. All three reviewer probes were re-run and agree. RED evidence was reproduced independently by reverting three hunks in an isolated copy: all three T81 tests fail there, worst shape 52004.5 ms. HOWEVER, verifying the structural fact from the pattern surfaced a third, pre-existing zero-click bypass: REFERENCE_DEF's `[^\]]+` capture cannot see a definition whose label carries a backslash-escaped `]`, which CommonMark permits and `marked` resolves; five spellings reach all four public boundaries with `redaction.state: "none"` and zero findings. That is blocking and reproduced at a public boundary, so it fires the scope decision's single exception and may not be filed as a residual. The other four findings are documentation-grade.

findings.impact: Zero-click exfiltration bypass in the mandatory floor. Five spellings (shortcut, short, full, collapsed, two-escape) each have `marked` emit while dispatchCallTool, prepareOutputForPersistence, validateOutputForTransport and redactToolOutput all carry the attacker host and report redaction.state "none". A non-empty allowlist does not help; the secrets floor masks only a secret-shaped parameter and leaves the attacker host and the fetch intact. Pre-existing (the same capture is at HEAD 0bc6418) but live on this tree, and it falsifies the completeness claim at policies.md:28 for the reference forms.

Rewrite the header comment at :707-717, which asserts the now-weakened fact. If out of budget for phase 1, flag every reference definition in a document containing `\]` inside a bracket run.

findings.problem: CommonMark matches link labels after context-insensitive Unicode case folding; normaliseLabel uses String.prototype.toLowerCase, which is context-sensitive. "ΟΣ".toLowerCase() is "ος" (U+03C2) where case folding gives "οσ", so `![οσ]` resolves against `[ΟΣ]: URL` under a folding renderer and not here.
findings.impact: Not reproduced with a fetching renderer. marked uses toLowerCase too and agrees with the detector on every sigma spelling driven (s13-s16, u3, u4); the only residue is textual — in u4FinalSigmaRev the attacker URL survives all four boundaries as plain text with no renderer fetching it. Reachable only against a strictly conformant folding renderer, which is outside the measured threat model.
findings.suggested_fix: None under this dispatch. If a later round widens the renderer set beyond marked, switch to case folding and apply it on both the definition and use sides in the same change, per the rule already recorded at exfil.ts:654.
